Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Verdant Energy Solutions Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants may press star then one on their touchtone phone if they would like to be placed in the queue. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Verdant Energy Solutions' results for the second quarter. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Development Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Verdant Energy Solutions had a transformative second quarter, reflecting our unwavering commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see surging demand for our clean energy solutions and are ideally positioned to seize the expanding market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, our overall performance highlights and key achievements stand out as record-breaking across multiple fronts. We posted revenue of $478 million, a 42% jump year-over-year and surpassing the upper end of our guidance by 8%. This momentum came from a 55% rise in energy sales from our 1.8 GW operational assets, plus $220 million from fresh engineering, procurement, and construction contracts. We're now lifting our full-year revenue outlook to $2.1 to $2.3 billion, signaling 35% to 45% growth. EBITDA reached $162 million at a 34% margin, up 450 basis points from last year, fueled by capacity utilization factors averaging 28% in our solar assets, outpacing industry norms of 22% to 25%. Adjusted earnings per share hit $0.72, exceeding estimates by 15%. Our development backlog has swelled to $6.2 billion, backed by 4.5 GW of locked-in projects through 2028 for superior visibility. Free cash flow jumped 60% to $110 million, supporting a new $500 million share repurchase program we unveiled today.

These figures ride the wave of U.S. Inflation Reduction Act benefits, where tax equity deals unlocked $350 million in investment tax credits this quarter, similar to NextEra Energy's approaches. In Europe, REPowerEU is speeding up power purchase agreements, with our solar projects' levelized cost of energy now under €30 per MWh, undercutting gas peakers. Operationally, we brought online 850 MW of solar PV using bifacial TOPCon modules from partners like LONGi and Trina Solar in Texas and California projects, including the flagship 400 MW Desert Bloom in the Mojave Desert, which hit commercial ops early and runs at a 32% capacity utilization factor thanks to our AI yield optimization tools. We also activated 300 MWh of long-duration battery storage at Ironwood with LFP cells from CATL blended with our VerdantFlow vanadium redox flow technology, avoiding 150,000 metric tons of CO2 equivalent through peak shaving and grid services in CAISO and ERCOT—roughly equal to removing 32,000 vehicles from roads. Wind added 200 MW in the Midwest with Vestas 15 MW turbines tuned for onshore winds, growing contributions 25% year-over-year.

Sustainability shines too: Year-to-date, our assets produced 2.8 TWh of clean power, offsetting 1.9 million tons of CO2 equivalent, with 100% uptime across SCADA-monitored sites. We're advancing toward SBTi-validated 1.5°C targets, holding Scope 1 and 2 emissions at 8 gCO2e per kWh. North America powered 68% of revenue with 50% growth from IRA-fueled hyperscaler deals like those with Google and Microsoft for 15-year PPAs tied to data centers; our Texas queue boasts 2 GW. EMEA delivered 22% via wins in Spain and Italy under the Net-Zero Industry Act, highlighted by a 250 MW agrivoltaics site in Andalusia with sheep grazing at €22 per MWh on a 20-year contract for difference. APAC made up 10% as we ramp a 500 MW pipeline in Australia under the Capacity Investment Scheme, using U.S. content for IRA alignment against China's module dominance.

Innovation drives us: VerdantEdge 2.0 edge-computing cuts O&M costs 18% via ML on decade-plus SCADA data. Our 50 MW Ironwood electrolyzer pilot generated 1,000 tons of green hydrogen from surplus solar, eyeing DOE grants like Plug Power's. We're shifting to firm assets—20% of backlog now BESS and hydrogen, aiming 50/50 by 2027—while pursuing M&A like our $250 million Midwest wind O&M acquisition. Supply risks like polysilicon swings are hedged with 24-month contracts and U.S. JVs. Q2 confirms our build-own-operate model amid BNEF's $1.7 trillion clean energy capex forecast by 2030, with H2 catalysts like 1.2 GW FID-ready projects.

Second, our operating capacity reached 5,850 MW by quarter-end, up 22% from 4,800 MW last year, thanks to commissioning 750 MW including the 350 MW Desert Sun Phase II solar in California's Imperial Valley, 250 MW Atlantic Breeze offshore wind off the East Coast, and repowering 150 MW Texas onshore wind from Vestas V90-3MW to V136-4.2MW for 15-20% annual energy production uplift. By technology: solar PV at 3,450 MW or 59%, up 28%, using First Solar Series 7 bifacials with 24% DC/AC ratios and Array Technologies trackers; onshore/offshore wind at 1,950 MW or 33% with 38% and 52% capacity factors via GE Haliade-X; BESS at 450 MW/1,050 MWh or 8%, highlighted by 200 MW/800 MWh Ironclad in PJM with Tesla Megapack 2XL. Excluding 2,200 MW under construction like the 1 GW Rajasthan solar, our backlog hits 12 GW.

Generation output climbed 26% to 4,650 GWh, yielding a 35.2% portfolio capacity factor topping U.S. averages by EIA data, exceeding P50 by 8% on strong resources. U.S. (72%) delivered 3,350 GWh up 32% with ERCOT at 42% wind factors and CAISO solar curtailment under 2%; Europe (18%) 840 GWh flat but with $15 million battery uplift; APAC (10%) 460 GWh up 45% on Australian/Indian hybrids. Despite 3% curtailment, our AWS ML platform for irradiance/wind prediction lifted AEP 5-7%, with 92% solar inverter and 95% BESS efficiency utilization. Hybrids now 15% of new capacity target 60%+ firm factors, tapping IRA PTC/ITCs for $450 million tax equity. Merchant hedged at 20%. Q3 eyes 4,900-5,200 GWh at 5,950 MW, full-year 18,500 GWh up 25%, backed by $2.5 billion capex for 7 GW by 2026 at 40% IRR.

Third, gross margins hit 28.5%, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 25.2% and 110 sequentially from 27.4%, our best since Q4 FY2022, blending transitory relief and structural gains. Input costs eased with polysilicon at $8-9 per kg from Tongwei/GCL-Poly versus $30 peaks, dropping N-type TOPCon BOM 15% to $0.22/W; silver paste down 8% via busbar tech like LONGi/JinkoSolar. Product mix shifted to bifacial TOPCon/HJT at 65% of shipments from 42%, with $0.31/W ASPs 12% above PERC, aided by 80% vertical cell/wafer ownership in Texas/Ohio fabs cutting logistics 20% amid China curbs. Utility-scale at 72% revenue locked $0.35/W PPAs like NextEra/Orsted. Americas margins 32% on IRA data center demand from Google/Microsoft with 10 cents/W adders; Europe 26% via REPowerEU; APAC 22% offset by India rooftops. Q3 eyes 29-30%, FY2024 27-28%.

Operating margins reached 12.3%, up 250 bps YoY from 9.8%, via gross leverage and OpEx at 16.2% of revenue down from 18.1%. R&D at $45 million (3.2%) birthed 24.8% HJT cells rivaling First Solar/Enphase; PERC consolidation cut overhead 18%, AI maintenance hit 92% utilization like Tesla Shanghai. SG&A at 4.8% shifted to EPC like 1.2 GW Duke deal; G&A 3.2%. U.S. 15% with $15M Section 45X; Europe 10% offset by Dutch subsidies; APAC 8% boosted by 25% battery bundles. 'America-First Scale' with $1.2B capex targets 25 GW by FY2026, 32-35% gross margins; 85% backlog visibility, 70% fixed EPC. Watch silver/EU CBAM, but 95% ESG chain and storage/hydrogen set 15%+ op margins by FY2025.

Fourth, PPA pricing trends show bifurcation from post-Ukraine unwind, supply moderation, and O&M inflation. Global utility solar PPAs down 15-20% to $24-32/MWh; U.S. Southwest at $26/MWh levelized from 22.5% PERC bifacials/trackers at $0.82/W EPC for 12%+ IRRs. ERCOT hybrids at $38/MWh blended with 5-7% escalations. Europe: German EEG under €25/MWh, Spanish €32/MWh, UK CfD £47/MWh. APAC: Australia AUD55/MWh, India ₹2.50/kWh. Our weighted new PPA $29/MWh. Extensions secured 2.1 GW of 7.8 GW eligible at 18% uplifts to $31/MWh average, like 20-year SCE rollover for 450 MW Gemini with curtailment shares. 82% success rate via tracker retrofits/AI soiling cuts, BESS pairings; Texas wind/NRG at 22% premium with Fluence storage. U.S. 90% capture in PJM; APAC 15% escalations; Europe 70% with funds. 'PPA 2.0' adds dynamic clauses/ESG ties; corporate PPAs 800 MW with Apple/NVIDIA, 22% new backlog. Pricing bottoms H2 at $27/MWh, up 8-10% 2025; $15.2B backlog 65% fixed to 2028 for $1.2-1.4B FCF by 2026.

Fifth, significant market trends profoundly shape us. Global adds hit 510 GW in 2023 per IEA, up 50%, solar 75%; 2024 at 560 GW, 30% generation share, LCOE under $30/MWh. Our 45 GW backlog up 35% QoQ, Aurora bifacials at 12% U.S. share, 28% margins. Storage exploded 75 GW/80% growth to $130/kWh LFP, VRFBs rising; our 25 GWh pipeline 40% backlog, 2.2 GWh Q2 at 42% margins like Tesla/PG&E. Policies: IRA $110B/140 GW, Europe 300 GW, China/India incentives. North America 55% revenue/$1.2B PPAs; Europe 25% growth via CBAM-qualified TOPCon; APAC 20% with HydraFloat 500 MWac. Supply stabilized polysilicon $8-10/kg, rare earths challenge met by 70% U.S. chain/-15% capex. Perovskite tandems near. Pillars: tech scale with $500M R&D/5% capacity lift; diversification via hyperscaler 10 GW/$45/MWh; green bonds/IRA for 12x returns. Renewables to 50% power by 2030/$2T TAM; hedges/queues manage risks for 25% CAGR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. We are pleased with our financial results for the second quarter. Revenue reached $478 million, representing a 42% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 28.5%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $77 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $85 million, or $0.72 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $500 million in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Now, I'll pass the call to Taylor Kim to discuss our project development pipeline.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 12 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Morgan Patel will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management—displacing 1.9 million tons of CO2 equivalent year-to-date while achieving 100% uptime and 8 gCO2e/kWh Scope 1/2 intensity toward SBTi 1.5°C goals. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability, like agrivoltaics blending solar with agriculture. We believe that our sustainability efforts not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Morgan. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. We will now open the lines for questions. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks for the question, Mike. Supply chain pressures have eased considerably but remain a watch point, particularly for polysilicon, TOPCon modules from China, and rare earths in offshore wind. That said, they've had minimal drag on our timelines this quarter—we commissioned 850 MW solar and 750 MW total on schedule or ahead, thanks to proactive hedging. We've built 24-month inventories, diversified to U.S./Tier 1 suppliers like First Solar and our own Texas/Ohio fabs covering 80% cell/wafer needs, slashing logistics 20% and dodging export curbs. For BESS, CATL LFP and Tesla Megapacks are locked via multi-year offtake, with VRFBs de-risking long-duration via domestic sourcing. Permitting risks like BOEM for offshore are offset by 18-month queues versus industry 24 months. Overall, this positions our 12 GW pipeline and 2,200 MW AUC—like Rajasthan—for on-time delivery, with $2.5B capex 60% equity-funded. We're on track for 7 GW adds by 2026 at 40% IRRs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets like India, Australia, and Brazil represent high-growth vectors, comprising 10-20% of our backlog with 45% output surges in APAC. Our playbook emphasizes localized partnerships—e.g., Adani for Rajasthan 1 GW solar, AGL for Australian 500 MW hybrids under Capacity Investment Scheme—and compliance tailwinds like India's SECI tenders at ₹2.35/kWh with transmission waivers, or Australia's NEM rooftop PPAs at AUD55/MWh amid coal phaseouts. We hedge China dominance with U.S. content for IRA/CBAM, deploying HydraFloat for 500 MWac floating solar. PPAs blend fixed strikes $29-36/MWh with escalators, corporates like NVIDIA for AI loads. M&A tuck-ins and green bonds fund scale, targeting 25% CAGR. Risks like LGC volatility or PLD auctions are managed via 82% extension success and 70% U.S.-style vertical integration. This diversification boosts resilience, with APAC pipeline ramping to 20% of adds by 2027.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, David. Competition is fierce with China's 85% module supply and peers like NextEra scaling, but we differentiate via vertical integration (80% owned production), premium tech like 24.8% HJT/23.5% bifacials at 65% mix commanding $0.31/W premiums, and AI platforms like VerdantEdge boosting AEP 5-7%, O&M down 18%, capacity factors to 35.2%. Our 45 GW backlog, $15.2B PPAs 65% fixed, and 82% extensions at 18% uplifts provide unmatched visibility versus peers' 65%. IRA/REPowerEU unlocks $450M tax equity/$1.2B PPAs; storage 40% backlog at 42% margins shields intermittency. 'America-First' $1.2B capex for 25 GW U.S. capacity targets 32-35% gross margins, while hybrids/firm assets hit 50/50 EBITDA split by 2027. ESG chain (95% compliant), SBTi targets, and hyperscaler deals (22% corporates) create moats. We're outpacing via execution—28.5% margins, 12 GW pipeline—for 25% CAGR amid $2T TAM.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Verdant Energy Solutions. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
